claim_type_rationale: The universe rule is deterministic and source-defined by closed canonical WWF designation: Wikipedia's `Global 200` master article enumerates the 51 priority ecoregions of the 'Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests' (TMBF) major habitat type, organized by 5 biogeographic realm headings (Afrotropical / Australasia / Indomalaya / Neotropic / Oceania). WWF Global 200 is a closed canonical curated list of ~238 priority ecoregions identified by World Wildlife Fund since 1997-1998 publication; the TMBF subset is stable. Universe membership = 'parent Global 200 entry listed in master article TMBF section' — no curator judgment for universe membership. Per-row cell values (Realm + Representative WWF Ecoregions + WWF Ecoregion Codes) are taken from the master article's consolidated TMBF-by-realm tabulation per cycle-3 audit's master-derived row-list dump (51 rows × 4 cells = 204 source-extractive values, all master-verbatim). Mirror precedents for closed-canonical-list source_defined with explicit set-filter (subset of larger curated list): `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (16-entry IAVCEI Decade Volcanoes closed list); `phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age` (12-period ICS Phanerozoic universe).

collection_summary.approach: Pre-curation design pass (3 rounds of pre-staging design review). This instance replaces an abandoned `major_tropical_rainforests_by_continent` design after 2 rounds of pre-staging on that design exposed structural universe-fuzziness — there is no closed canonical 'major tropical rainforests' authoritative list (curator-bounded 'major' selection would have required candidate_rebuild + multi-round audit churn). Pivot path: audit cycle-2 of major_tropical_rainforests recommended pivoting to WWF Global 200 TMBF subset (closed canonical curated list). Cycle-1 of the Global 200 design (this instance's cycle-1) drafted a 4-col schema with country/4th-cell plans; cycle-2 audit found 4 BLOCKING issues (universe granularity parent-vs-child / realm vocab incomplete / country cell not master-supported / no reliable 4th value cell) and recommended a 4-col schema using master-structural fields (parent entry PK + realm + child-ecoregions semicolon-delim + WWF codes semicolon-delim). Cycle-3 audit dumped the exact 51-row master-derived list (correcting the row count from cycle-2's 50→51, Indomalaya 17→18) — this dump was used verbatim at cycle-0 staging to avoid the decade_volcanoes-style cycle-1 BLOCKING factual catch on best-guess cell mismatches. 3-round pre-staging review precedent matches `major_world_lakes_per_continent` arc for fuzzy-universe pivots.
collection_summary.partition_structure: Closed canonical 51-entry WWF Global 200 TMBF universe with explicit biogeographic-realm scope. Per-realm distribution: Afrotropical 11 + Australasia 8 + Indomalaya 18 + Neotropic 12 + Oceania 2 = 51 parent Global 200 entries. Single PK Global 200 Ecoregion (parent entry labels).
collection_summary.row_count_check: 51 rows match the master-derived count per cycle-3 audit's row-list dump. The 5-realm vocabulary (Afrotropical / Australasia / Indomalaya / Neotropic / Oceania) is locked per master section headings; Palearctic / Nearctic / Antarctic have no TMBF entries because tropical moist broadleaf forests don't exist in those realms — explicitly out of scope.

roles.role_note: universe: enumerates the closed canonical 51-entry WWF Global 200 TMBF list with explicit conformance to WWF Global 200 priority ecoregion designation. value: supplies Global 200 Ecoregion parent labels + Realm (section headings) + Representative WWF Ecoregions (child ecoregion labels listed under each parent) + WWF Ecoregion Codes (codes listed next to children) cell values for all 51 staged rows via the master article's TMBF-by-realm consolidated section.

validation_cross_checks.rationale: No validation cross-checks documented for this instance. Per cycle-3 audit confirmation: the master Wikipedia `Global 200` article supplies all 4 cells (Global 200 Ecoregion + Realm + Representative WWF Ecoregions + WWF Ecoregion Codes) directly via its consolidated TMBF section. Per-ecoregion Wikipedia articles exist but are NOT needed for cell-value grounding — master tabulation is sufficient. This is the cleanest source_count=1 source plan in pkdb_bench (single master with no validation prose needed). Mirror precedent: `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` source_count=1 with master-only validation.

source_coverage_notes.source_grounding_summary: 1 registered source (Global_200: roles = [universe, value]). No additional validation cross-checks documented — master article carries 100% of cell-value grounding via its TMBF-by-realm tabulation per cycle-3 audit confirmation.

decision_log.decision: claim_type = source_defined (closed-canonical-list WWF Global 200 TMBF 51-entry universe)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-3 audit confirmation: 'claim_type=source_defined: yes, if staged as the 51 parent Global 200 TMBF entries.' WWF Global 200 is a closed canonical curated list maintained by World Wildlife Fund since 1997-1998 publication. The TMBF subset (51 entries) is stable and source-defined by master article's TMBF section enumeration. No curator judgment for universe membership; no curator judgment for cell values (all 4 cells master-verbatim). Distinct from candidate_rebuild (no curator-bounded universe selection) and partially_supplemented (no rebuilding of master subset). Mirror precedent: `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (16-entry IAVCEI closed list) + `phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age` (12-period ICS Phanerozoic universe).

decision_log.decision: Universe granularity = parent Global 200 entries (NOT child WWF ecoregions)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit BLOCKING #1 + cycle-3 confirmation: 'I recommend parent Global 200 entry as PK because that is the closed Global 200 unit and keeps row count moderate.' Child WWF ecoregions number in the hundreds (~238 total across all biomes); parent Global 200 entries are the closed canonical curated subset. Parent-entry granularity yields 51 rows for the TMBF biome subset. Child ecoregions go in the `Representative WWF Ecoregions` semicolon-delim value cell + their codes in `WWF Ecoregion Codes`.

decision_log.decision: Realm vocabulary locked to 5 closed values: Afrotropical / Australasia / Indomalaya / Neotropic / Oceania
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit BLOCKING #2 + cycle-3 confirmation: my cycle-1 design proposed 4-value vocab (Afrotropic / Australasia / Indomalaya / Neotropic) — cycle-2 audit caught two errors: (a) missed Oceania entries (South Pacific Islands forests + Hawaii moist forests are in Oceania realm); (b) master spelling is 'Afrotropical' NOT 'Afrotropic'. Corrected to 5-value closed vocab matching master section headings.

decision_log.decision: Schema = 4 cols (Global 200 Ecoregion PK + Realm + Representative WWF Ecoregions semicolon-delim + WWF Ecoregion Codes semicolon-delim)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit BLOCKING #3-4: my cycle-1 proposed schema included Primary Sovereign States (not uniformly master-supported) and a 4th value cell (Habitat Subtype / Area / Biodiversity Feature — none master-supported). Cycle-2 audit recommended the 4-col schema with source-structural fields: parent entry PK + realm section heading + child ecoregion labels + WWF codes. All 4 cells are master-extractive per cycle-3 audit's row-list dump. Semicolon-delim convention for multi-value cells matches existing pkdb_bench precedents.

decision_log.decision: Row count = 51 (NOT 50 as proposed in cycle-2)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-3 audit's required correction: 'the master-derived universe is 51 rows, not 50. Counts are 11 + 8 + 18 + 12 + 2 = 51 parent Global 200 entries.' My cycle-2 design followed audit's preliminary 50-row count from cycle-2's enumeration; cycle-3 audit's careful re-count corrected Indomalaya from 17 → 18, yielding 51 total. Cycle-0 staging used the cycle-3 master-derived row-list dump verbatim (51 rows).

decision_log.decision: Source plan = source_count=1 (master only, no validation cross-checks)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-3 audit confirmation: 'source_count=1: yes, the Global 200 master supplies all four cells.' This is the cleanest source-plan in pkdb_bench — single master with no per-ecoregion validation prose needed. Mirror precedent: `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` source_count=1 with master-only validation (per-volcano articles registered as validation prose). Here per-ecoregion articles exist but are NOT needed for cell-value grounding since master tabulation suffices.

decision_log.decision: Entity class = physical-features/ecoregions (NEW fine-class extending physical-features bucket from 8 → 9)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-3 audit confirmation: 'physical-features/ecoregions is better than abstract-categories; these are named geographic conservation units.' Ecoregions have defined geographic boundaries per WWF — physical-features matches the real-geographic-unit framing. NEW fine-class extending physical-features bucket from 8 instances (mountains, rivers×2, deserts, islands, oceanic-trenches, lakes, volcanoes) to 9. NOT abstract-categories/ecoregions (would mirror periodic_table_groups conceptual-classification precedent but ecoregions are physically-defined, not conceptual-only).

Per cycle-3 audit confirmation: 'Domain: Environment/Conservation is the best fit.' Environment family currently at 1 instance only (`countries_over_50pct_renewable_electricity`, Environment/Energy); this brings to 2 with NEW Conservation subdomain. Crisis-light Environment family chip 1 → 2 — one of 4 families at exactly 1 instance (Health, Law, Food, Environment). WWF Global 200 is explicitly a conservation-priority list, so Environment/Conservation is the semantically correct subdomain over Environment/Forests or Environment/Ecology.

decision_log.decision: Category = geographic primary + set_filter secondary; operation_type = filter
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-3 audit confirmation: 'Category=geographic primary, secondary_category=set_filter, operation_type=filter are defensible.' Geographic primary because the 51 entries are organized by biogeographic realm (uneven per-realm distribution emphasizing geographic-conservation-priority shape). Set_filter secondary because the universe is set-filtered to (a) Global 200 priority designation + (b) TMBF major habitat type biome. Operation_type filter mirrors `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (set-filter by IAVCEI list) + `phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age` (set-filter by Phanerozoic Eon).

decision_log.decision: Sort = Realm ASC alphabetic primary + Global 200 Ecoregion ASC alphabetic secondary
decision_log.rationale: Curator sort convention — master's row order is master-internal (parent entries within each realm in WWF Global 200's own listed order, not alphabetic). Cycle-0 staging applied curator alphabetic-within-realm sort for consistent benchmark ordering. Mirror precedent: `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` uses alphabetic-within-continent sort even though master display order differs.

Cycle-1 design of major_tropical_rainforests_by_continent attempted curator-bounded 'major rainforests' universe selection with candidate_rebuild claim_type; cycle-1 audit found 4 BLOCKING issues (universe rule not obeyed by preview / mixed entity types / master doesn't define universe / dual area cells fragile). Cycle-2 audit recommended pivot to Global 200 TMBF for source_defined defensibility. This instance is the post-pivot replacement — same picker motivation (chip geographic gap-2 + crisis-light Environment family + NEW physical-features fine-class) but with closed canonical source-defined universe replacing the fuzzy 'major' curator-bounded selection. Lesson for future: when a 'major X' framing yields universe-fuzziness, pivot to a closed canonical authoritative list (WWF / IAVCEI / ICS / IUPAC / Conservation International) — same precedent path as decade_volcanoes_by_continent (which replaced an abandoned vaccines design after 5 rounds of pre-staging review).

normalization_decisions.rule: Parent entry label verbatim per Wikipedia master `Global 200` article's TMBF section row labels. 51 closed values per cycle-3 audit's master-derived row-list dump. Some entries use ' moist forests' suffix (Sulawesi moist forests / Moluccas moist forests / etc.); some use ' montane forests' suffix (Albertine Rift montane forests / Cameroon Highlands forests / etc.); some use compound names (South Western Ghats montane rain forests and moist deciduous forests / Maldives–Lakshadweep–Chagos Archipelago tropical moist forests). Locked verbatim to master — no curator normalization or shortening.

Closed 5-value categorical per master section headings: Afrotropical / Australasia / Indomalaya / Neotropic / Oceania. Per cycle-2 audit BLOCKING #2: master spelling is 'Afrotropical' NOT 'Afrotropic' (common ecology-textbook variant). Other 3 realms not in vocabulary because they have no TMBF entries: Palearctic / Nearctic / Antarctic. Note: WWF's full 8-realm scheme includes Palearctic (temperate Eurasia/N.Africa), Nearctic (temperate N.America), and Antarctic in addition to the 5 used here — the latter 3 have no tropical moist broadleaf forest ecoregions in Global 200 because the biome doesn't exist in those temperate/polar realms.

Semicolon-delimited list of child WWF ecoregion labels listed under each parent Global 200 entry in the master TMBF section. Each parent entry has 1-7 child ecoregions per the master's hierarchical structure (some parents are single-child like Albertine Rift montane forests → only Albertine Rift montane forests AT0101; others span multiple children like New Guinea montane forests → 4 children AA0105/AA0107/AA0120/AA0127). Delimiter is '; ' (semicolon + space) per pkdb_bench precedent for multi-value cells (mirror: `west_side_story` co-director multi-value cell). Cell values verbatim per cycle-3 audit's master-derived row-list dump — includes en-dash (Cross–Sanaga–Bioko), comma-bearing names (São Tomé, Príncipe, and Annobón forests — quoted in CSV), and special-character names (Choco–Darien moist forests). NO curator paraphrasing.

Semicolon-delimited list of WWF ecoregion codes listed next to child ecoregion labels in the master. Codes follow the WWF convention: 2-letter realm prefix + 4-digit ID. Realm prefixes: AT (Afrotropical) / AA (Australasia) / IM (Indomalaya) / NT (Neotropic) / OC (Oceania). Each row's codes are aligned positionally with the Representative WWF Ecoregions cell (1st code = 1st child ecoregion, 2nd code = 2nd, etc.). Delimiter is '; ' (semicolon + space) matching the Representative WWF Ecoregions delimiter. Cell values verbatim per cycle-3 audit's master-derived row-list dump.

open_questions.question: If WWF revises the Global 200 list (e.g., adds or removes TMBF entries), should the instance be re-staged?
open_questions.answer: Yes, when WWF officially publishes a revised Global 200 list with TMBF-section additions/removals/relabelings, this instance can be extended or revised. Universe is locked to WWF Global 200 as of cycle-3 audit's master-extraction date (2026-05-18). temporal_sensitivity = low reflects that Global 200 revisions are rare and small. Wikipedia's master `Global 200` article tracks WWF's published list with periodic updates.

open_questions.question: Should the schema include WWF biome label as a 5th cell (all values = 'Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests')?
open_questions.answer: No — Biome = TMBF for all 51 rows is constant and provides zero information. The instance title + universe rule already establish the TMBF-biome scope. Schema kept at 4 cols (Global 200 Ecoregion / Realm / Representative WWF Ecoregions / WWF Ecoregion Codes).

open_questions.question: Should pre-Phanerozoic-realm Palearctic / Nearctic / Antarctic entries be in scope (with empty/N/A status)?
open_questions.answer: No — those 3 realms have NO TMBF entries in WWF Global 200 because tropical moist broadleaf forests don't exist in temperate/polar realms. Universe is locked to the 5 realms with TMBF entries (Afrotropical / Australasia / Indomalaya / Neotropic / Oceania).

open_questions.question: Why didn't the major_tropical_rainforests_by_continent design work?
open_questions.answer: Cycle-2 audit of that earlier design found 4 BLOCKING issues: (a) universe rule not obeyed by my preview (Daintree below threshold + 'seasonal' not rainforest); (b) rows mixed entity types (large systems vs ecoregions vs regional complexes vs mountain ranges vs local forests); (c) master `Tropical rainforest` article doesn't define a row universe (it gives broad regions not a canonical list); (d) Current/Original Area cells were high-risk exact-match targets. Cycle-2 audit recommended pivot to closed canonical WWF Global 200 universe — adopted in this instance. Lesson: when 'major X' framing yields universe-fuzziness, pivot to a closed canonical authoritative list (WWF Global 200, IAVCEI, ICS, IUPAC, Conservation International).

open_questions.question: Why use semicolon-delimited child cells instead of a separate row per child ecoregion?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-2 audit recommendation: parent Global 200 entries are the closed canonical curated unit (51 entries); child ecoregions are the WWF base-level units (~238 across all biomes). Staging at parent granularity keeps row count moderate (51) and matches the Global 200 curation philosophy. Children are documented in the Representative WWF Ecoregions cell + WWF Ecoregion Codes cell as semicolon-delim multi-value cells. Mirror precedent: pkdb_bench has multi-value semicolon-delim cells in `films_winning_at_least_8_academy_awards` (West Side Story co-director field 'Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins').
